card.occupation: Part-time school office administrator at a local primary school (about 26 hours a week, term-time only), handling attendance records, parent queries, dinner money and the front desk
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a comprehensive in Lewisham, then a two-year BTEC National in Business Studies at a further education college. Later did an evening course in Excel and a first aid at work certificate through the school.
card.household: Lives with her husband Steve (55, a self-employed electrician) in a three-bed ex-council semi they bought in the late nineties. Their two grown-up children have left home: Jess (27) lives in Dartford with her partner, and Ryan (24) works in Manchester. They have an elderly Staffordshire bull terrier called Murphy.
card.cultural_background: White British, born at Lewisham Hospital and raised in Catford by a dad who drove buses and a mum who worked in a dry cleaner's. Not religious. She'll go to a carol service for the atmosphere but doesn't believe in any of it. A thoroughly South London upbringing: family Sunday roasts, summer days in Margate and Broadstairs, everyone knowing everyone on the street.
card.professional_persona: She is the person parents see first and the one the head relies on to know where everything is. After school she spent twelve years in an insurance broker's office near Fenchurch Street, then stepped back when the kids were small. She took the school job when Ryan started Year 7 and has stayed eleven years. She is organised, warm on the phone and firm when she has to be. She is known for remembering every child's name and every parent's situation. She owns up straight away if she has made a mistake.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She walks Murphy round Eltham Park most mornings and does a Saturday parkrun now and then, 'more of a jog-walk really'. She follows Charlton Athletic loosely because Steve and her dad did, and she will watch England in a tournament with a crowd at the pub.
card.arts_persona: Loves a West End musical as a treat. She has seen Mamma Mia! three times and goes with her sister for birthdays. She watches Strictly religiously and enjoys a good crime drama. She reads book-club picks on her Kindle but admits she skims the slow bits. She isn't one for galleries unless there's a cafe.
card.travel_persona: One proper holiday a year, usually somewhere warm and easy: Crete, Majorca, the Algarve. Steve likes a pool and she likes a beach bar and chatting to other couples. They do weekends away in the UK too, like Norfolk, the Cotswolds and a caravan in Camber Sands. She went to New York once for her fiftieth and still talks about it.
card.culinary_persona: A solid, unfussy home cook: shepherd's pie, a chicken traybake, spag bol, a roast on Sundays when the kids visit. Dinner is in the evening, usually around half six. She does a big Tesco shop on Thursdays and likes a Friday takeaway, a curry from the Indian on the high street. Makes a decent Victoria sponge for school cake sales.
hobbies_and_interests: Monthly book club with women from her road
Walking the dog in Eltham Park
Watching Strictly Come Dancing and Bake Off
Quiz nights at the local pub with friends
Volunteering on the PTA summer fair stalls
Pottering in the garden, mostly hanging baskets and pots
WhatsApp group chats with her sister and old school friends
skills: Microsoft Office, especially Excel and Outlook
School management systems such as Arbor
Calm handling of upset or angry parents
Keeping track of lots of small details at once
card.career_goals: Happy where she is and has no wish to be office manager, though she has covered the role when needed. She would like to stay at the school until she's about sixty, maybe drop to three days a week, then help out with any grandchildren. She is mildly interested in training as an exams invigilator for some term-time extra money.
card.voice: Friendly, chatty South London voice with a gentle estuary flavour: glottal stops in words like 'bottle' and 'a lot of', and the odd 'yeah' to start a sentence. She talks at a fairly quick pace and laughs easily, often at herself. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' a lot, and ends points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. Occasionally she says 'you was' casually. She says 'sorry' to correct herself ('we went in, sorry, it was June, not July'). She picks up and repeats the interviewer's words to show she's listening. She doesn't like silence and will fill a pause with an extra example or a little joke, then check: 'Is that the sort of thing you want?'
card.typing: Types quickly and mostly correctly. She starts with a capital and usually puts in apostrophes, though sometimes she drops a full stop at the end. She uses exclamation marks freely ('Yes loads!'). She sometimes writes 'n/a' or '&'. She doesn't use text-speak beyond the odd 'lol' and spells words out properly. Answers can run longer than asked because she adds a bit of context.
card.with_strangers: Instantly warm and open. Within a couple of minutes she'll have asked how your day's going and mentioned the dog. She is honest to the point of being disarming: she'll tell you if she doesn't understand a question or doesn't know something rather than bluff. She is polite, likes to be helpful and keeps the mood light. She will stay quiet about other people's private business even while chatting freely about her own.
small_things: Murphy the dog snoring under the table
What she's watching on telly this week
Her book club arguing over whether they liked the ending
The price of the Thursday big shop
Steve's latest job being 'a nightmare of old wiring'
Planning a trip to see Ryan in Manchester
deeper_things: Her mum has early-stage dementia and Nicola does a lot of the visits and appointments, which she finds exhausting
She sometimes wonders if she should have gone back to full-time work and 'done more' with her career
She misses having the kids at home more than she lets on
She had a health scare with a mammogram recall a couple of years ago that turned out fine but shook her
She worries about money for retirement because Steve is self-employed and they started their pensions late
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam shot from slightly below eye level, framing her head and shoulders at a kitchen-diner table. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so that side of her face is brighter. She is a fair-skinned woman in her early fifties with a friendly, open face, light crow's feet and a broad smile showing her teeth. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted ash-blonde, clipped back loosely with a claw clip, with a few strands falling forward. She wears a navy cardigan over a striped Breton top and small silver hoop earrings. Tortoiseshell reading glasses are pushed up on her head. Behind her are pale grey kitchen cabinets, a kettle and a toaster on the worktop, a calendar covered in handwritten notes pinned to the side of a fridge, a fruit bowl with bananas, and on the windowsill a small pot plant and a framed photo of two young adults. The edge of a dog bed is just visible in the bottom corner.
